## What The Business Is

Walmart Inc. is a global, people-led and tech-powered omnichannel retailer headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas, operating retail stores, wholesale clubs, eCommerce websites and mobile apps across the U.S., Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico. Its reportable segments are **Walmart U.S.**, **Walmart International** and **Sam’s Club U.S.**; Walmart describes its purpose as helping customers “save money and live better,” serving about **280 million customers and members weekly** through **10,900+ stores** and digital properties in **19 countries**, with FY2026 revenue of **$713 billion** and about **2.1 million associates**. ([stock.walmart.com](https://stock.walmart.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000104169-26-000102/wmt-20260430.htm))

## What It Does

Walmart sells grocery, general merchandise, health and wellness items, fuel and other categories through large-format stores, neighborhood formats, Sam’s Club membership warehouses, marketplaces, pickup, delivery and digital channels. In Q1 FY2027, Walmart U.S. net sales were led by grocery at **$70.7 billion**, followed by general merchandise at **$26.4 billion** and health and wellness at **$16.4 billion**; Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales were about **$27.1 billion**, while Sam’s Club U.S. eCommerce sales were about **$4.1 billion**. The company is also building higher-margin adjacent businesses including advertising, marketplace, fulfillment services, membership and data/commerce-media capabilities. ([stock.walmart.com](https://stock.walmart.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000104169-26-000102/wmt-20260430.htm))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Walmart’s Q1 FY2027 results, reported May 21, 2026, showed consolidated revenue of **$177.8 billion**, up **7.3%** year over year, with operating income up **5.0%** and adjusted EPS of **$0.66**; management reiterated FY2027 guidance for constant-currency net sales growth of **3.5%–4.5%**, adjusted operating income growth of **6%–8%**, and adjusted EPS of **$2.75–$2.85**. ([stock.walmart.com](https://stock.walmart.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000104169-26-000095/0000104169-26-000095.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The transcript highlights continued omnichannel momentum: enterprise eCommerce grew **26%**, Walmart U.S. marketplace net sales grew nearly **50%**, U.S. store-fulfilled delivery more than doubled over two years, and more than **36%** of U.S. store-fulfilled deliveries were completed in under three hours. Management also said Walmart can reach roughly **60% of the U.S. population in 30 minutes or less**, reinforcing the store network as fulfillment infrastructure. ([corporate.walmart.com](https://corporate.walmart.com/content/dam/corporate/documents/newsroom/2026/05/21/walmart-releases-q1-fy27-earnings/q1-fy27-earnings-call-transcript.pdf))

Higher-margin businesses are scaling. In Q1, global advertising grew **37%**, Walmart U.S. advertising grew **36%**, membership fee revenue rose over **17%**, and Walmart later announced a more unified global commerce-media strategy across Walmart Connect U.S., Walmart Connect International and Sam’s Club Connect. ([corporate.walmart.com](https://corporate.walmart.com/content/dam/corporate/documents/newsroom/2026/05/21/walmart-releases-q1-fy27-earnings/q1-fy27-earnings-call-transcript.pdf))

Walmart also extended its speed and value positioning: it announced 30-minute-or-less delivery across **33 U.S. markets**, passed **1 million drone deliveries** across 66 stores in four states and five metro markets, and in early July lowered prices on thousands of seasonal grocery and household items. ([corporate.walmart.com](https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2026/05/28/walmart-brings-30-minute-or-less-delivery-to-33-us-markets))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Fuel and consumer pressure were prominent headwinds. Management said Walmart absorbed about **$175 million**, or roughly **250 basis points** of operating-income growth, from higher-than-planned fuel costs in global distribution and fulfillment; executives also noted U.S. consumers were feeling pressure and warned that if elevated costs persist, Walmart would expect somewhat higher retail price inflation in Q2 and the second half of FY2027. ## Bull Case
- Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 7.3%, with eCommerce up 26%, marketplace up ~50%, advertising up 37%, and membership fees up 17% — a growing mix of high-margin, capital-light income streams that supports both FCF growth and a premium multiple.
- Guidance reiterated: 3.5–4.5% constant-currency sales growth and 6–8% adjusted operating income growth; if capex intensity moderates after the recent supply-chain/fulfillment build-out, FCF could rebound sharply toward $15B+.
- Store-as-fulfillment infrastructure (60% of U.S. population reachable in 30 minutes) is a durable moat that justifies the market's willingness to pay ~66–75x FCF over the past year.

## Bear Case
- TTM FCF has declined three years running ($14.8B → $13.9B → $12.7B) despite revenue growth, reflecting heavy capex; the current 75x EV/FCF is very rich for a low-single-digit-growth retailer.
- Fuel cost absorption (~$175M, ~250bps drag on operating income growth), a pressured consumer, and warned price inflation in H2 FY2027 threaten margin progress; the stock already fell >7% on profitability concerns.
- FCF/EV yield of 1.33% is well below the 3-year average of 2.21%; mean reversion toward ~45x FCF would imply an EV near $600B and severe downside.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $12,669M. Guidance implies 6–8% operating income growth, but capex remains elevated and fuel/inflation headwinds persist. I assume a modest ~5% FCF recovery, giving forward FCF ≈ **$13,300M**.
- **Applied multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~75x (1/0.01332); the 1-year average is ~66x (1/0.01509). I apply a blended **71x**, allowing slight compression from today's rich level while acknowledging the durable premium the market has assigned to Walmart's omnichannel/advertising mix.
- **Forward EV:** 13,300 × 71 ≈ **$944,300M**.
- **EV-to-market-cap bridge:** Current gap = 951,094.1 − 887,644.1 = $63,450M (net debt). Forward market cap = 944,300 − 63,450 ≈ **$880,850M**, roughly flat versus today — growth in FCF offset by modest multiple compression.
